proposals.before: Gaozu, temple name the Sagely Literary, Sagely Military, Resplendent and Solemn, Filial Emperor, was of the Liu clan and originally named Zhiyuan. His forebears were Shatuo; his family later settled at Taiyuan.
proposals.after: Gaozu, posthumous name the Sagely Literary, Sagely Military, Resplendent and Solemn, Filial Emperor, was of the Liu clan and originally named Zhiyuan. His forebears were Shatuo; his family later settled at Taiyuan.
proposals.reason: 睿文聖武昭肅孝皇帝 is the posthumous name; 高祖 is the temple name, so calling the long honorific a temple name is incorrect.

proposals.before: In ancient usage, the first month of the year was not called “first month” either; it was called the first, or correct, month.
proposals.after: In ancient usage, the first month of the year was likewise not numbered as “one”; it was called the Correct Month.
proposals.reason: Chinese 不云一，而曰正月 means they did not say “one,” but said zhengyue (Correct Month); the idiomatic contradicts itself by denying then affirming “first month.”

proposals.before: The Discourses of the States, speaking of the six pitch-pipes, says yuan comes between and dalu; the Zhouyi, listing the six lines, says initial nine.
proposals.after: The Discourses of the States, speaking of the six pitch-pipes, says Yuanjian and Dalu; the Zhouyi, listing the six lines, says initial nine.
proposals.reason: 元間大呂 names the pitch Yuanjian with Dalu; reading 間 as “comes between” is a mistranslation of the pitch name.
